varieties.description: Features rigid, puckered, dark green leaves with a unique texture.

care.water: Water every 1-2 weeks, allowing soil to dry out between waterings. Expect to water more often in brighter light.
care.light: Thrives in bright to medium indirect light. Not suited for intense, direct sun.
care.soil: A rich, nutrient-dense potting soil that retains moisture but drains well. A mix of peat, perlite, and pine bark is ideal.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

varieties.name: Monstera Lechleriana
varieties.description: A beautiful Monstera species (Lechleriana) that adds tropical flair to any indoor garden.

care.water: Water every 1-2 weeks, allowing soil to dry out between waterings. Expect to water more often in brighter light.
care.light: Thrives in bright to medium indirect light. Not suited for intense, direct sun.
care.soil: A rich, nutrient-dense potting soil that retains moisture but drains well. A mix of peat, perlite, and pine bark is ideal.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

varieties.description: A beautiful Monstera species (Spruceana) that adds tropical flair to any indoor garden.

care.water: Water every 1-2 weeks, allowing soil to dry out between waterings. Expect to water more often in brighter light.
care.light: Thrives in bright to medium indirect light. Not suited for intense, direct sun.
care.soil: A rich, nutrient-dense potting soil that retains moisture but drains well. A mix of peat, perlite, and pine bark is ideal.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

varieties.name: Monstera Deliciosa ‘Compacta’
varieties.description: A distinct variety of the classic Monstera Deliciosa, known for its iconic split leaves.

care.water: Water every 1-2 weeks, allowing soil to dry out between waterings. Expect to water more often in brighter light.
care.light: Thrives in bright to medium indirect light. Not suited for intense, direct sun.
care.soil: A rich, nutrient-dense potting soil that retains moisture but drains well. A mix of peat, perlite, and pine bark is ideal.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

care.water: Drought tolerant — water only when the soil is fully dry (every 2–3 weeks). Overwatering causes rot; water sparingly in winter.
care.light: Adapts from low light to bright indirect; brighter light speeds growth and tolerates a little direct sun.
care.soil: Free-draining cactus/succulent mix. Never let it stand in water.
care.toxicity: Mildly toxic to cats and dogs; can cause nausea if eaten.

varieties.name: Sansevieria Laurentii
varieties.description: The most popular Snake Plant variety with yellow margins on its upright green leaves.

care.water: Allow soil to dry out completely between waterings. Very drought tolerant.
care.light: Can tolerate low light to direct sunlight.

varieties.name: Sansevieria Zeylanica
varieties.description: Features dark green leaves with light gray-green horizontal stripes.

care.water: Water sparingly. Let soil dry completely. Susceptible to root rot if overwatered.
care.light: Adaptable to almost all light conditions, from low light to full sun.

care.water: Soak-and-dry: water thoroughly, then let the soil dry out completely before watering again. Much less in winter dormancy.
care.light: Bright light with several hours of direct sun. Stretched, leggy growth means it needs more light.
care.soil: Gritty, fast-draining cactus mix with sand or pumice. Always use pots with drainage holes.
care.toxicity: Most are non-toxic, but some (e.g. Euphorbia) have irritating sap — keep those away from pets.

varieties.name: Echeveria
varieties.description: Rose-shaped succulents available in many colors.

varieties.name: Jade Plant
varieties.description: Tree-like succulent symbolizing good luck.

varieties.name: Aloe Vera
varieties.description: Medicinal succulent known for soothing skin burns.

care.water: Keep the soil lightly and evenly moist; never let it dry fully. Sensitive to tap-water minerals — use filtered or rainwater.
care.light: Medium, indirect light. Direct sun fades the markings and crisps the leaf edges.
care.soil: Rich, moisture-retentive yet well-draining mix. Loves high humidity (60%+).
care.toxicity: Non-toxic and pet-safe — a great choice for homes with cats and dogs.

varieties.name: Calathea Medallion
varieties.description: Known for its large, round, medallion-like leaves with intricate patterns of green and silver.

care.water: Keep soil consistently moist but never soggy. Use distilled or filtered water to avoid leaf tip burn.
care.light: Low to Medium indirect light. Direct sun will fade the patterns.
care.soil: Peat-based potting mix that holds moisture but drains well.
care.humidity: High humidity (60%+) is essential. Use a humidifier or pebble tray.

varieties.name: Rattlesnake Plant (Calathea lancifolia)
varieties.description: Features long, slender leaves with dark green spots and wavy edges, resembling a rattlesnake's markings.

care.water: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Sensitive to fluoride in tap water.
care.light: Low to Medium indirect light.

varieties.name: Calathea Ornata (Pinstripe Plant)
varieties.description: Dark green leaves with thin pink stripes that look like they were painted on.

care.water: Keep moist. Do not let dry out completely.
care.light: Medium indirect light. Too little light fades the pink stripes.
care.humidity: Very high humidity needed to prevent crisping edges.

care.water: Water when the top 3–5 cm dries out, roughly weekly. Drooping means thirsty; yellowing means overwatered.
care.light: Bright to medium indirect light. Tolerates lower light but grows slower; avoid direct sun.
care.soil: Loose, well-draining aroid mix with bark and perlite. Climbing types like a moss pole.
care.toxicity: Toxic to pets and people if ingested (calcium oxalate); sap may irritate skin.

varieties.name: Heartleaf Philodendron
varieties.description: A classic vining plant with heart-shaped dark green leaves. Very easy to care for.

care.water: Allow top 50% of soil to dry out between waterings.
care.light: Low to Bright indirect light. Very adaptable.

varieties.name: Philodendron Brasil
varieties.description: A cultivar of the heartleaf philodendron with lime green and yellow variegation down the center of the leaf.

care.water: Water when top inch is dry.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light to maintain variegation.

varieties.name: Pink Princess Philodendron
varieties.description: Rare and stunning climbing philodendron with dark leaves splashed with bright pink variegation.

care.water: Allow top inch to dry. Do not overwater.
care.light: Bright indirect light is crucial for pink color.
care.soil: Aroid mix (chunky, airy soil with orchid bark and perlite).

care.water: Let the top half of the soil dry between waterings — the thick leaves store water. Prone to rot if kept too wet.
care.light: Bright, indirect light. Tolerates medium light; variegated types need it brighter.
care.soil: Light, airy, well-draining mix (perlite/orchid bark). Likes a snug pot.
care.toxicity: Non-toxic and safe around pets and children.

varieties.name: Watermelon Peperomia
varieties.description: Leaves resemble the rind of a watermelon with silver and green stripes.

care.water: Allow soil to dry out almost completely. Stores water in leaves.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Peperomia Hope
varieties.description: A trailing variety with small, round, succulent-like leaves.

care.water: Let dry out between waterings.
care.light: Low to Medium indirect light.

varieties.name: Raindrop Peperomia
varieties.description: Features large, glossy, raindrop-shaped leaves.

care.water: Water sparingly when soil is dry.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

care.water: Water when the top few cm dry out and keep it consistent. Sudden changes or drafts cause leaf drop.
care.light: Bright, indirect light; rubber plant and fiddle-leaf take gentle morning sun. Rotate for even growth.
care.soil: Rich, well-draining potting mix. Dislikes being moved around frequently.
care.toxicity: Mildly toxic to pets; the milky sap irritates skin and stomach.

varieties.name: Fiddle Leaf Fig
varieties.description: Popular indoor tree with large, violin-shaped leaves.

care.water: Water when top inch is dry. Consistent watering schedule is key.
care.light: Bright indirect light to some direct morning sun.

varieties.name: Rubber Plant (Ficus elastica)
varieties.description: Sturdy plant with thick, glossy, dark green or burgundy leaves.

care.water: Keep soil moist but not soggy.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Ficus Audrey
varieties.description: The national tree of India, featuring velvety green leaves and white veins. Easier than the Fiddle Leaf.

care.water: Allow top inch to dry out.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

care.water: Let the top half of the soil dry; water every 1–2 weeks. Use filtered water — fluoride/chlorine causes leaf-tip browning.
care.light: Medium to bright indirect light. Tolerates lower light with slower growth; avoid direct sun.
care.soil: Loose, well-draining potting mix. Let it dry between waterings to prevent rot.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested; keep out of reach.

varieties.name: Dracaena Marginata (Dragon Tree)
varieties.description: Spiky, upright leaves with red edges on slender canes.

care.water: Allow top 50% of soil to dry. Sensitive to fluoride.
care.light: Low to Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Dracaena Lemon Lime
varieties.description: Vibrant neon yellow and green striped leaves.

care.water: Water when top inch is dry.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light for best color.

care.water: Keep soil lightly moist but never soggy; water when the surface feels dry. Avoid wetting the leaves to prevent mildew.
care.light: Bright, indirect light. Rex/foliage types prefer medium indirect light; flowering types like a touch more.
care.soil: Light, well-draining mix rich in organic matter. Enjoys humidity.
care.toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs — the tubers/roots most of all.

varieties.name: Rex Begonia
varieties.description: Grown for its stunning, multicolored, textured foliage.

care.water: Keep soil slightly moist. Avoid getting water on leaves.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Begonia Maculata (Polka Dot)
varieties.description: Angel wing shaped leaves with silver polka dots and red undersides.

care.water: Allow top inch to dry.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

care.water: Keep evenly moist in the growing season — water when the top 2–3 cm dries. Cut back sharply in winter when it may go dormant.
care.light: Bright, indirect light for strong leaves; avoid harsh direct sun.
care.soil: Chunky, well-draining aroid mix. Loves warmth and high humidity (60%+).
care.toxicity: Highly toxic to pets and humans — oxalate crystals cause painful swelling.

varieties.name: Alocasia Polly
varieties.description: Arrowhead-shaped dark green leaves with bold white veins.

care.water: Keep soil consistently moist but never soggy.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Alocasia Black Velvet
varieties.description: Small, velvety, almost black leaves with white veins.

care.water: Allow top inch to dry. Susceptible to root rot.
care.light: Medium to Bright indirect light.

varieties.name: Alocasia Zebrina
varieties.description: Known for its zebra-striped stems and arrowhead leaves.

care.water: Keep moist, not wet.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

care.water: Keep lightly moist; water when the top 2–3 cm dries. Fast-growing and thirsty in summer — don't let it dry out completely.
care.light: Bright, indirect light keeps the purple/silver colours vivid; it fades and gets leggy in low light.
care.soil: Standard well-draining potting mix. Pinch the tips to keep it bushy.
care.toxicity: Mildly toxic; sap can irritate the skin of pets and people.

varieties.name: Tradescantia Zebrina
varieties.description: Fast-growing trailing plant with purple and silver striped leaves.

care.water: Water when top inch is dry.
care.light: Bright indirect light to maintain purple color.

varieties.name: Tradescantia Nanouk
varieties.description: Compact variety with thick leaves featuring pink, white, and green stripes.

care.water: Water from bottom to avoid leaf rot. Allow to dry slightly.
care.light: Bright indirect light.

care.water: Water when the top 2–3 cm of soil dries; keep lightly moist, not soggy. Loves humidity.
care.light: Bright, indirect light for the best blooms. Too little light means fewer flowers; avoid direct sun.
care.soil: Coarse, very well-draining aroid mix (bark + perlite) — the roots need air.
care.toxicity: Toxic to pets and humans — calcium oxalate causes mouth and throat irritation.

care.water: Keep soil lightly moist in summer; let the top 2–3 cm dry in winter. Avoid both drought and sogginess.
care.light: Medium to bright indirect light. Pink/variegated types need it brighter to hold colour; avoid direct sun.
care.soil: Well-draining, peat-based mix with perlite. Add support if you want it to climb.
care.toxicity: Toxic to pets and people if chewed (calcium oxalate).

care.water: Allow the top 2–3 cm to dry between waterings, roughly weekly. Reduce in winter; avoid waterlogging.
care.light: Bright, indirect light. Tolerates medium light; direct sun scorches the leaves.
care.soil: Rich, well-draining potting mix with peat and perlite.
care.toxicity: Toxic — sap causes temporary numbness/swelling of the mouth (hence 'dumb cane'). Keep from pets and children.

care.water: Extremely drought tolerant — water only when the soil is completely dry (every 2–3 weeks). Overwatering is the main killer.
care.light: Low to bright indirect light; one of the best plants for low-light rooms. Avoid direct sun.
care.soil: Well-draining potting mix; let it dry fully between waterings.
care.toxicity: Toxic to pets and humans if ingested; sap can irritate skin.

care.water: Keep soil consistently moist — it wilts dramatically when dry but revives quickly after watering. Never let it dry out fully.
care.light: Medium, indirect light. Direct sun fades the veins and burns the leaves.
care.soil: Moisture-retentive, well-draining mix; thrives in high humidity — great for terrariums.
